clue.text: Consider track before bash in place for social activities

parts.note: to count someone as something is to consider them so
RY, short for railway, is a track for trains
to club someone is to bash them

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up a run along a track before going to a party somewhere sociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the railway ahead of the bash.
explanation.definitionFit: A country club is a members' establishment offering sports, dining and other leisure pursuits.

clue.text: Unimportant person misused 23 of the same kind

parts.note: a cog in the machine is a minor functionary

indicators.note: something misused is put to the wrong purpose, so the letters of the referenced entry are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 23 down

explanation.surface: A minor figure has misapplied entry 23 to something similar.
explanation.walkthrough: A clue number in the wordplay stands for that entry's answer, here ANTE, a stake in poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate words or things are related by common origin, hence alike in nature.

clue.text: Brussels right about supporting cycling nut? False

indicators.note: cycling sends things round and round, so the letters of the nut get moved about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means turning round, so the Brussels-and-right pair is read from the end back

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cyclist's loose nut prompts a false claim about Brussels' rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts the reversed EU and R underneath the rearranged nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue and false are plain synonyms for something not in accordance with fact.

clue.text: Actors aren't sad cast includes soldier undergoing a break-up?

indicators.note: includes means the soldier is taken inside the other letters
to cast is to throw, and thrown letters land in a new arrangement
a break-up scatters things, so the soldier's letters are split apart too

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Cheerful performers in a cast that takes on a soldier whose relationship is ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier does not stay in one piece: G and I end up apart, which is why the clue adds that he is undergoing a break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragedians are performers of tragic roles, so they are a kind of actor.

clue.text: What many a fen may make you, rainy at intervals

definitions.text: What many a fen may make

indicators.note: at intervals means taking letters spaced out, every other one

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A soggy fenland landscape and what it might make of you on a wet day.
explanation.walkthrough: The fen is not marshland: it is a Chinese coin, a hundredth of the main currency unit.
explanation.definitionFit: One hundred fen make one yuan, the basic unit of Chinese currency.

clue.text: Severely criticise essayist and master without limits

indicators.note: with no limits means the word's boundary letters at each end are dropped

parts.note: Charles Lamb, the English essayist who wrote as Elia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reviewer savaging a writer and his teacher, both without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb is the crossword's favourite essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambaste someone is to berate or attack them harshly in words.

clue.text: Good to visit Gulf state, ignoring hotel deal

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so good's letter is placed within the country
ignoring something leaves it out, so one letter of the country goes

parts.note: a kingdom in the Persian Gulf
Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A traveller heading for Bahrain skips the hotel and finds a better deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an agreement or transaction between parties, which is a deal.

clue.text: Maybe cryptic indication of "eat meal"

parts.note: surface reading: a note on how a crossword might signal a word
setter's reading: a late-afternoon meal whose name, read as a clue, tells you to make TEA 'high', ie scramble it, to get the word eat

explanation.walkthrough: The answer works backwards as a clue: 'high' is an anagram signal, and tea jumbled spells eat.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is a substantial early-evening meal in Britain, usually with cooked food alongside the tea.

clue.text: Reheating cooked wraps for instance, which is comforting

indicators.note: to wrap something is to enclose it, so the short phrase goes inside
cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
as in 'such as', introducing an example

explanation.surface: Warming up leftovers in a tortilla, say, as a soothing kitchen ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heart-easing relieves anxiety or sorrow, which is to say it gives comfort.

clue.text: Respected naval officer changing sides for Aled

indicators.note: Aled split down the middle has two sides, and one side is swapped for the other

parts.note: the senior rank in a navy
the name halves into a left side AL and a right side ED; the right replaces the left

explanation.surface: An esteemed admiral switches allegiance in favour of someone named Aled.
explanation.walkthrough: Aled is a Welsh first name, as in the singer Aled Jones; its two halves are AL and ED, and AL at the end of the officer becomes ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Admired and respected both mean held in high regard by others.

clue.text: Macron's score in superlatively boring examination

indicators.note: in places the French number inside the superlative adjective

parts.note: dry means dull, and driest is its superlative
Macron is the French president, so his score, twenty, is in French

explanation.surface: The French president's results in a deeply dull exam.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty; naming a Frenchman signals the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving test is the practical examination a learner must pass to get a licence.

clue.text: Hiding deed mostly, mistreats adders

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it inside, so the shortened deed sits within the other word

parts.note: to abuse is to mistreat

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone who ill-treats snakes while concealing what they have done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adders' are not snakes but things that add up.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame of beads used for arithmetic, so it is a device for adding.

clue.text: Endless battle for meat

indicators.note: endless means losing the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the sea battle of 480 BC in which the Greeks defeated the Persians

explanation.surface: An unending fight over food.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, seasoned sausage, a kind of preserved meat.

clue.text: Democrat last to give speech restricting American commitment

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the American letter is held inside the speech word

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat

indicators.note: last to points at the final letter of the next word only

parts.note: the final letter of give
diction is manner of speaking
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A US politician pledging himself in a final speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedication is devotion to a cause or task, which is a commitment.

clue.text: Quaint note about cruciverbalists

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the musical note goes round the other piece

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
setters and solvers of this puzzle can call themselves we

explanation.surface: A rather sweet message written about crossword fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruciverbalists are crossword people, so the setter includes himself and the solver: we.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for affectedly dainty or quaint, sweetly old-fashioned.

clue.text: Amateurs in comeback, it papers over talent surprisingly

indicators.note: papering over something covers it, so the reversed piece wraps around the reworked word
surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
ID means identity papers

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the short pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dabblers staging a comeback, where publicity covers up a lack of talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it papers' is read backwards as one string, then split so its halves bracket the rearranged talent; ID is the usual crossword shorthand for identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilettanti, the Italian plural, are dabblers in the arts who lack professional commitment, ie amateurs.

clue.text: Gives fine wordplay, is he setter's starting point?

parts.note: a pun is a form of wordplay
taken as written

indicators.note: a starting point is where something begins, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of setter

explanation.surface: A solver wondering whether a setter begins with good wordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' reads as praise for the wordplay, but it belongs with 'Gives' as a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish is to impose a penalty, and a fine is one such penalty.

clue.text: A ship is boarded by peacekeepers arresting base, finally treacherous assistant

indicators.note: arresting means seizing and holding, so the peacekeepers take the base letter inside
a ship boarded by people has them inside it, so those letters go within the ship and is

parts.note: taken as written
a man is a ship, as in man-of-war or merchantman
United Nations peacekeeping forces
e is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of treacherous
taken as written

explanation.surface: UN forces board a vessel and arrest a treacherous helper.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN plus IS takes in UN-holding-E followed by S.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a literary assistant who takes dictation or copies manuscripts.

clue.text: Flat battery's part includes yttrium and nitrogen

indicators.note: includes means the two element symbols are placed inside the battery part

parts.note: the positive terminal of a battery
Y is the chemical symbol for yttrium
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A dead battery's component turns out to contain two chemical elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' reads as describing a dead battery, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means bland and inoffensive, so dull or flat in character.

clue.text: Mislaying bar is flipping tedious

indicators.note: flipping turns something over, so the small word is removed in backwards order
bar means except, so the following letters are taken out

parts.note: to mislay something is to lose it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Losing a pub is, in British slang, flipping boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British intensifier on tedious, but it turns is into SI, which is then removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Long can mean dull through excessive length, as in a long afternoon.

clue.text: Rich work university supplied

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
U is the abbreviation for university
lent means provided or supplied

explanation.surface: A wealthy project bankrolled by a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy or lavish, synonyms of rich.

clue.text: Uncertainty around a small business creates disaster

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word for uncertainty runs backwards

parts.note: an if is a doubt or uncertainty
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small
CO is short for company

explanation.surface: Doubt surrounding a little firm leads to its collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, a complete disaster.

clue.text: Satirical press uncovered vice

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A satirical newspaper exposes wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' wants to be newspapers; it is the domestic chore of ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironic writing says the opposite of what it means to mock, which is a satirical method.

clue.text: Student feeling time has gone to get freedom

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: has gone means is no longer present, so that letter drops out

parts.note: an attitude is a feeling or opinion
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A student feels that once their time is served they will be free.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Ts in the feeling goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is scope for free action or thought, a degree of freedom.

clue.text: Poet loses head in bet

indicators.note: losing its head means the word's opening letter is chopped off

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet

explanation.surface: An Italian poet gambles and is beheaded for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake each poker player puts in before the deal, so a bet.

clue.text: Dull ring with no echoes for imaginary animal

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so every one of the letters named is removed

parts.note: grey means dreary and dull
to ring someone is to phone them
Echo is E in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A dull ring without reverberation, set beside a fantastical beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The gryphon, or griffin, is a mythical beast with an eagle's head and a lion's body.

clue.text: Core of app covered by bug check

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside, so the middle letter goes within the creature

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so just the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the centre letter of app

explanation.surface: A software bug lies at the heart of an app, so check it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' reads as a software fault; here it is a creepy-crawly.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, which is to check.

clue.text: "Behind second" in French is "le plus à l'est"?

indicators.note: in places the first pair of words inside the French verb

parts.note: est is French for is
a mo is a moment, a second
astern means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A French lesson translating a phrase about position on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself French, meaning the furthest east.
explanation.definitionFit: Le plus à l'est is French for the most to the east, which is easternmost.
